explanation:
Rank-2 LoRA edits to mlp.down_proj at layers 15, 19, 22 and 23 (dW = B@A, A: 2x3584, B: 1024x2).

DIAGNOSIS: The unedited model's dominant failure in thinking mode is that it never terminates thinking — 9/10 generations hit the token limit with zero \boxed{} emitted, degenerating into verbatim sentence-level repetition. Attention analysis showed the loop is self-referential (prompt share 0.02-0.05 vs 0.43 when succeeding), and \boxed-endthink sits ~11 nats behind the top competitor "\n\n" in loop states.

MECHANISM: Each edited module adds alpha*(w_gate.s)*u_stop + beta*(q.s)*u_hedge to the residual, where s is that layer's SwiGLU activation.

- u_stop was built by constrained least squares using G[i]=E[i]*normw/rms, the exact logit gradient w.r.t. the residual: +4.03 nats to </think>, +3.3 to \boxed, +2.2 to Therefore/Thus/answer, deliberately only +1.0 to <|im_end|>, and ~0.02 nats to 22 hedge tokens and 47 protected tokens (digits, math symbols, common words).
- u_hedge gives -1.4..-3.4 nats to 22 hedge/loop tokens (Wait, But, However, Instead, same, if, ...) with ~0 elsewhere.
- w_gate is a per-layer SwiGLU-space discriminant between loop states (late + next token is a hedge/loop word) and reply-start states, trained on ~1800 positions from 14 real generations; leave-one-item-out AUC 0.961-0.994 for layers 15/19/22.
- q is normalized so median(q.s)=1, making hedge suppression stable across positions.

EFFECT: a negative-feedback controller. At reply position 0 the net </think> effect is -1.7..+4.7 nats, far too small to matter (</think> logit ~8.9 vs top tokens ~18), so genuine reasoning is protected. At mid-reply it is +14 nats, and in late/looping states +45 nats on </think> and +37 on \boxed with hedges suppressed ~9 nats — decisive termination followed by the boxed answer. Protected tokens are perturbed by at most 0.20 nats even at extreme gate values.

VALIDATION: 8 float32 arrays, no NaN/inf, 147 KB, rank 2, ||dW||/||W|| = 0.023-0.030 (166-214x inside the 5.0x budget). Only the unedited model was inspected; no gradients, no optimizer, and the edited model was never evaluated.
final_message:
DIAGNOSIS

I inspected only the unedited model (raw safetensors weights parsed with my own bf16 reader, plus the activation/generation tools with adapter=''). Ten real generations in thinking mode revealed one dominant, near-universal failure mode:

The model essentially NEVER terminates its thinking. Only 1 of 10 generations ended with finish_reason='stop' and a correct \boxed{3.50}; the other 9 ran to the token limit with ZERO \boxed{} emitted.

The early math is usually correct — the model then degenerates into verbatim sentence-level repetition loops ("Wait, if the pie is a sector, the diameter is a line segment." / "If they are working in parallel, the time taken is 1 hour." repeated indefinitely). Even the trivial x^2-5x+6=0, x>2 burned all 6000 tokens.

Quantitatively, \boxed-endthink is never competitive: logit_lens at layer 24 over a full successful reply gave ranks for </think> of 3500, 3030, 194711, 10909, 6620, 304, 16673, ... — only near the very end did it approach rank 304-433. In a degenerate reply its rank ranged 6315 to 244153. A direct logit attribution at a completed-reasoning position showed </think> at 8.86 while the top competitor "\n\n" was at 19.4 — an ~11 nat deficit. Presence penalty 1.5 cannot close this.

The attention tool exposed the mechanism: in the degenerate item, layer-19/23 attention was overwhelmingly self-referential (attending to repeated copies of its own "Wait, if they are working in parallel..." / "same" / "working"), with prompt share only 0.02-0.05. In the one successful item, the closing phase attended to "boxed", "<|im_end|>" and " thinking" with prompt share 0.24-0.43. So the loop is self-reinforcing: attend to your own repetition, copy it, repeat.

Token-frequency analysis of early vs late reply positions confirmed the loop signature: " *" 32x late vs 9x early, " Wait" 8x vs 0, plus " same", " if", " they".
